q: Does the CBAM 50 tonne exemption cover hydrogen imported into Antwerp?
title: Hydrogen imports and the 50 tonne exemption
short: No. The 2025 simplification exempts importers bringing in 50 tonnes or less a year of covered goods, but hydrogen and electricity are excluded from that exemption. Any hydrogen import, however small, needs an authorised declarant, its direct embedded emissions and certificates.
audience: Chemical companies and energy importers in the Antwerp and wider Benelux chemical cluster

p: Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 replaced the old per-consignment value threshold with a yearly mass threshold per importer: up to 50 tonnes of covered goods a year in total is exempt. Hydrogen and electricity do not count towards it and are not exempted by it.

Hydrogen under CN 2804 10 00 is charged on direct emissions only. For hydrogen made from natural gas, that is the CO2 from reforming and fuel; electricity used in electrolysis is indirect and not charged under Annex II today.
Ammonia imported as a hydrogen carrier is its own CBAM good under 2814 and does count towards the 50 tonne threshold. Large cargoes exceed it in any case.
